title: The Art of Hedging in Academic Writing
text:
Hedging refers to a set of linguistic devices that writers use to qualify a claim or to signal uncertainty. In academic writing, phrases such as 'it seems likely' or 'the data may suggest' allow researchers to present their findings without overstating them. Such language reflects an awareness that scientific knowledge is provisional and open to revision. Consequently, hedges are regarded as essential rather than merely cautious.

Critics, however, argue that excessive hedging can obscure a writer's actual position and weaken the force of an argument. A text saturated with qualifications may leave readers unsure which claims the author genuinely endorses. For this reason, skilled writers calibrate their hedges carefully, reserving them for claims that truly warrant caution. Ultimately, the art lies in balancing precision with humility.

questions.text: According to paragraph one, what is the purpose of hedging phrases such as 'it seems likely'?
options: To present findings without overstating them
To prove that every claim is absolutely certain
To replace the need for evidence

questions.text: According to paragraph two, what can excessive hedging do to an argument?
options: It can make the argument more forceful
It can obscure the writer's actual position
It can remove all uncertainty from a text
It can eliminate the need for citations

questions.text: What can be inferred about skilled writers from paragraph two?
options: They use hedges selectively, where caution is justified
They hedge every sentence to be safe
They rarely think about how readers will interpret their claims

questions.text: What is the main idea the passage implies about good academic writing?
options: Certainty is always preferable to caution
Hedging is useful only in the natural sciences
Good writing balances precision with appropriate caution
Critics have proven that hedging is harmful

vocabulary.definition: to make something unclear or hard to see
to adjust something carefully so that it is accurate
to deserve or require a particular response

paragraph_translations: Los recursos de atenuación (hedges) son un conjunto de recursos lingüísticos que los escritores usan para matizar una afirmación o indicar incertidumbre. En la escritura académica, frases como 'parece probable' o 'los datos podrían sugerir' permiten a los investigadores presentar sus hallazgos sin exagerarlos. Este lenguaje refleja la conciencia de que el conocimiento científico es provisional y está abierto a revisión. En consecuencia, estas atenuaciones se consideran esenciales y no simplemente prudentes.

Sin embargo, los críticos sostienen que el exceso de atenuación puede oscurecer la posición real del escritor y debilitar la fuerza de un argumento. Un texto saturado de matices puede dejar a los lectores inseguros sobre qué afirmaciones defiende realmente el autor. Por eso, los escritores hábiles calibran sus atenuaciones con cuidado, reservándolas para las afirmaciones que realmente justifican cautela. En última instancia, el arte consiste en equilibrar la precisión con la humildad.
